components.description: FMLA leave as implemented by Drexel policy HR-33: up to 12 weeks of unpaid, job-protected leave in a rolling 12-month period for the employee's own serious health condition (including pregnancy and post-partum disability), the birth and care of a newborn, adoption or foster placement, or care of a seriously ill spouse, child or parent.
components.faculty_group_note: "all eligible Faculty and Professional Staff Members"; Faculty Member defined as "tenured, tenure-track, non-tenured track or adjunct position who teaches within any college, school, center or institute in the University"
components.eligible_parent_wording: "the birth and care of a Faculty or Professional Staff Member's newborn child"; "own chronic health condition, including disability due to pregnancy and/or post-partum"; "placement of an adopted son or daughter or a foster child"; "FMLA applies equally to all Faculty and Professional Staff Members regardless of gender"
components.entitlement_note: A statutory entitlement (FMLA) restated by the policy: "may be entitled to up to twelve (12) weeks"; "Each spouse is entitled to 12 weeks".
components.duration_note: "up to 12 weeks ... in a rolling 12-month period"; FMLA taken in the previous 12 months is subtracted. The statute states 12 workweeks (29 U.S.C. 2612(a)(1)).
components.service_requirement: employed by Drexel for at least twelve months (consecutive or not) and at least 1,250 hours (60% FTE) in the prior twelve months
components.dual_employee_rule: each spouse is entitled to 12 weeks of FMLA leave for the birth and care of their newborn child
components.time_window: leave for the birth and care of a child must conclude within 12 months after the birth or placement
components.notice: at least 30 days prior written notice of the proposed leave; as soon as practicable when advance notice is not possible
components.medical_certification_note: Required where the leave is based on a serious health condition of the employee or an immediate family member; recertification may be required every 30 days. Not stated for birth-and-care leave.
components.relief_note: Stated: "relieved of all work duties and are not required to perform any duties for the duration of their leave".

sequence.note: R3b: discretionary teaching relief for both academic terms when the leave spans two terms contains the leave.

notes: Reference date 2018-02-22. The five usable sources: 2018_00_link.txt (HR-33 Family and Medical Leave, governing faculty leave policy, Wayback 2018-02-11); 2018_01_tenure_promotion_policy_rev2010.txt (Tenure & Promotion Policy rev. May 19, 2010); 2018_02_hr3901_non_fmla_medical_leave_2017.txt (HR-39.01, effective October 2017); 2018_03_hr72_short_term_disability_2017.txt (HR-72); 2018_04_hr37_long_term_disability_rev2013.txt (HR-37).

Under the rule for records with no governing document (reader instructions §3): HR-33 (a leave policy covering 'tenured, tenure-track, non-tenured track or adjunct' faculty) and the Tenure & Promotion Policy (a tenure-clock policy) are governing documents for faculty leave, so missing is false.

Drexel has no dedicated paid parental or maternity leave in the saved documents. The faculty benefit for a birth is FMLA leave (12 weeks) with salary continuation (6 weeks after year one, 12 after year two; U8 two-year member: 12 weeks), discretionary teaching relief for both terms when the leave spans two terms, the non-FMLA medical leave (90 calendar days in 12 months, FML time counted against it), employee-paid STD, university-paid LTD, and an automatic one-year tenure extension for a primary caregiver.

Calendar: HR-33 and HR-39.01 define full-time faculty by 'three or more quarters'; the 'academic terms' are quarters, so calendar.kind = quarter (R8, Drexel example), and the term length follows R8's order.

Birth parent chain: FMLA leave 12 weeks (c1) with salary continuation 12 weeks within it (c2); non-FMLA medical leave 90 calendar days concurrent with FMLA (c6), with employee-paid STD within it from week 2 to day 90 (c8); both leaves within discretionary teaching relief for both terms when the leave spans two terms (c3, c7, concurrent); LTD from day 91 (c9, no duration).

Non-birth parent chain: FMLA leave 12 weeks (c1) with salary continuation 12 weeks within it (c2); non-FMLA medical leave 90 calendar days concurrent with FMLA (c6); both within discretionary teaching relief for both terms when the leave spans two terms (c3, c7, concurrent).

HR-33 says that faculty 'not eligible for salary continuation for the duration of their leave' may use short-term disability if they purchased coverage; for the two-year member salary continuation covers the 12 FMLA weeks. STD is employee-paid (R1d) and counts in no paid figure.

HR-33 restates the tenure extension as 'automatic' after each live birth or adoption without the primary-caregiver condition and refers to the Tenure and Promotion Policy, which governs; c4 is coded primary caregiver from the governing policy.

Not components: HR-33 and HR-39.01 'no extra duties above his/her normal workload shall be expected or required' before and after the leave (a workload protection with no relief); benefits continuation during leave (health insurance, life insurance, LTD, retirement contributions); LTD's statement that the department 'is not obligated to keep the ... position beyond the 90 calendar day period of disability' (consistent with the 90-day medical leave).

Cross-referenced but not saved: the Human Resources 'Leave of Absence' guidelines; 'FMLA FAQs'; 'Initiating a Claim with Guardian [PDF]'; Drexel's Attendance Policy (staff); the Academic Calendars webpage (tenure calendars); academic-unit tenure and promotion policies; AAUP Policy Documents and Reports (10th ed., 2006) and the 'Recommended Institutional Regulations on Academic Freedom and Tenure' (dismissal standards). The 'Policies 1-16' cross-references for the tenure policy are page footers ('Drexel University Academic Policies'), not separate documents.

Statute verification: FMLA 12 workweeks checked against statute text 2026_00_us_fmla_29usc2612 (2612(a)(1)); eligibility (1,250 hours) against 2026_01_us_fmla_29usc2611_definitions.txt; intermittent/reduced schedule by agreement, 2612(b)(1). Pennsylvania has no baseline rows; no Pennsylvania statute is named in the documents.
